pr_title: Fix double click in CJK characters and create unit test
pr_body:
Fixes #75808 -> selecting chinese, japanese and korean characters with double click. The problem was with the external library UBreakIterator.
Solution: Check manually if the character is cjk.

pr_comments: @KoBeWi Hi! If there aren't any problems with my fix, I would kindly ask a review. Thank you!
The actual issues seems to be in `TextServer::shaped_text_get_word_breaks` and `TextEdit`, not in the ICU iterator.

To summarize my findings:
- There's an issue in `shaped_text_get_word_breaks` that can result in missing words.
- There's an issue in `TextEdit` which prevents selecting single character words by double-clicking.
- ICU iterator without setting locale to specific language with `@lb=strict` will add break after every CJK character, it's OK for line breaking, but probably not desired for word selection.
- Adding changes from this PR will prevent a lot of line breaks, so it's not a suitable fix. Also, different types of breaks are already marked and known after ICU iterator, so there's no need to hard-code character check (there are a lot more CJK character ranges beside used in this PR). It should be possible to modify `shaped_text_get_word_breaks` to skip non-space/punctuation breaks, which should be better for word selection (and won't change line breaking).

I'll do PR tomorrow (includes some public API changes to keep old behavior accessible, so require compact wrapper).

>There's an issue in TextEdit which prevents selecting single character words by double-clicking.

- There is a separate issue for this https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/89551
- and it's fixed in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/89556
Superseded by #90732. Thanks for the contribution!

issue_context.title: Double clicking CJK text does not select the word under the cursor
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.2.stable

### System information

Arch Linux

### Issue description

Double clicking on text selects the word under the cursor.

Try double clicking words below in the browser to see the expected behavior:

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	var variable := "test string"
	var عامل := "سلسلة الاختبار"
	var מִשְׁתַנֶה := "מחרוזת בדיקה"
	var 变量 := "测试 字符串"
	var 変数 := "テスト 文字列"
	var 변수 := "테스트 문자열"
```

This is the actual behavior in the script editor, doubling clicking on CJK text does nothing:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/372476/230700739-e82c7f18-baa0-462d-a08a-414c9a66cd30.mp4


It's true that Chinese and Japanese don't use spaces to separate words. Word breaking `字符串` (string) into `字符` (character) and `串` (sequence) is a completely different area of expertise. I think it should at least use spaces as word boundaries.

### Steps to reproduce

Use the test script above.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A

Hi! I'm a computer science student from Portugal currently completing a course where I have to choose an open source project, choose a bug, and then fix it with a pull request.

I have been looking into this and found out that in the function `shaped_text_get_word_breaks` (from the file text_server.cpp), `l_gl` seems to have duplicated words, i. e. `l_gl[i].start` and `l_gl[i].end` are the same as `l_gl[i + 1].start` and `l_gl[i + 1].end`, and `l_gl[i + 1].flags` are `GRAPHEME_IS_VIRTUAL`, `GRAPHEME_IS_SPACE` and `GRAPHEME_IS_BREAK_SOFT`, instead of just `GRAPHEME_IS_VALID`. Here's a video showing it:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/93451864/9471a4af-32db-4445-bb4f-c3b41f275329

So the root of the issue is probably in the function `shaped_text_sort_logical`
I will continue to look into this
